title: What is known about 1RB0LE_0LC0RA_1LE0RD_0RB---_0LF0LD_1LA0LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_0LC0RA_1LE0RD_0RB---_0LF0LD_1LA0LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. Its tape is single 1s separated by gaps of one, two or three 0s, and it grows to the left. At its visits to the left end a prefix made of the word 0 0 1 grows by one word each time while the time between visits roughly doubles, then shrinks back: the behavior of a counter. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Its events are decoded: a binary counter at the left end (3-cell digits) gains 1 per event and a 2-bit counter M right of a fixed 46-cell word gains 1; this is proved in Lean for every carry length. When M wraps, a slower counter further right changes (not decoded), and now and then the fixed words themselves are rebuilt.

New, 14 November 2026. The whole run is now one rule: the tape is a binary counter with doublers (words 1010, 000, 100), and each round sends one defect through it. A tape with one defect cannot halt; a halt needs two defects to meet. In 100,000 rounds there was no halt, and in the 4,500 rounds followed word by word every defect disappeared long before the next one started. Whether that is always so is the open question.

New, 22 November 2026. Lean now proves that a tape with at most one defect cannot halt, so a halt needs a defect that survives its round. A new engine followed the defect word by word through 500,000 rounds (more than 2944,371 steps): every defect died about halfway into the tape. The top of the counter is now understood exactly: its layers are the binary expansions predicted by the conserved value, 1/15 − c·2−k/2/127. The defect only ever eats the irregular bottom layer; whether it can cross all of it in one round is the open question.

Later on 22 November 2026. Lean now also proves that the four visit functions are runs of the real transition table, and the round law. So the machine never halts from blank tape if every round's defect dies in its round; that one statement is all that is left.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 275 cells have been visited and 85 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text: A, B, C and D cross runs of the words 01, 10, 001 or 100 rightwards in one state, rewriting each copy the same way, for any number of copies and any surrounding tape.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator runs 10<sup>9</sup> steps without a halt.

claims.title: Visits to the left end
claims.text: At the visits of E to the left end on blank the tape is E>0 0 1 (0 0 1)^k 0 1 … followed by single 1s with gaps of one to three 0s. k grows by 1 from one visit to the next while the time between visits roughly doubles, and drops back now and then (to 8 at step 4,121,436; to 2 at step 109,450,476, after reaching 18).

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: A closed tape language with windows of 6 cells (found and checked by bbtools.ctl, not yet in Lean) allows a halt only with D reading a 1 at the left end of the tape, followed by 100100, 100101, 101001 or 101010.

claims.title: A counter
claims.text: A word per visit and twice the time per word is the signature of a binary counter whose digits are the gaps; the drops of k are its carries reaching further into the tape.

claims.title: The rule
claims.text: How the gaps encode a number, and what a visit does to it, are not known.

claims.title: The event rule (non-wrapping events)
claims.text: From L 0 0 0 (1 0 0)^k ENGINE A> 0 PREFIX [M] R (ENGINE = 00101001010100, PREFIX the 46-cell word 1001010100100101010010001001000100100010101010, M two 4-cell digits 1000 = 0 / 1010 = 1, low first) the machine reaches the same shape with the left counter + 1 (1 0 0 (0 0 0)^k) and M + 1, for M = 0, 1, 2, every k and every tape L, R (8k + 608 or 8k + 616 steps); also when the k ones reach the left end of the tape (the counter gains a digit). Nothing right of M is read.

claims.title: Events in the run
claims.text: With this ENGINE and PREFIX, events run from step 78,415 (left counter 32, M = 1): 110 consecutive events add 1 to both counters (27 of them wraps of M), up to left counter 142; then the PREFIX is rebuilt (one of the drops of the left-end count noted above).

claims.title: The wrap of M and beyond
claims.text: When M wraps, a slower counter right of M (4-cell words 0101/0100 and others) changes; how, and how the PREFIX is rebuilt, is not decoded. A halt (D reading 1) can only come in those steps, never inside a non-wrapping event.

claims.title: The run as rounds of one function
claims.text: On the mirrored tape, a visit of A (the head at a cell in state A until it first steps left of it) is a function on the half tape, and four such functions (A, E, F, P) close up. From [A] 0 0 S the machine returns to [A] 0 0 S' one cell further out with S' = 1 0 A(S). Derived by local simulation and checked against direct simulation of the machine.

claims.title: No halt in 100,000 rounds
claims.text: The visit engine, with visit counts kept as sums of powers of two, ran 100,000 rounds without a halt; the counts reach 187,512 bits. Only 7 window rules of A and E are ever used.

claims.title: A counter with doublers and one travelling defect
claims.text: In the words L = 1010, O = 000, I = 100 the function A is a binary counter (O, I the digits) in which every carry crossing an L becomes two. Each round adds one defect (a 10, 1 or 0 that does not fit the words), which travels through the counter, rewrites it, and disappears where it turns 1 I O into O L. A tape with at most one defect cannot halt (now proved in Lean, lean/Total.lean); a halt needs two defects side by side. The token rules reproduce the exact tape cell for cell (rounds 5 to 24), and in every round from 13 to 4,500 the defect disappeared about 40% of the way into the tape, long before the round ended.

claims.title: Does every defect disappear in time?
claims.text: If the defect of every round disappears before the round ends, the machine never halts. Where it disappears depends on the digits of the counter, which look irregular; no proof.

claims.title: A conserved value
claims.text: a value of the tape (each digit 1 counts 2-b, b = doublers minus digits before it, with corrections for the defect) grows by exactly 1 with every visit of A, with or without a defect: proved in Lean for the token rules (lean/Tokens.lean), and checked with exact fractions on every round. At the start of each round it is 1/15 up to about 2-k/2: the far end of the tape is the binary expansion of 1/15, I O O O repeated k/8 times.

claims.title: The one missing lemma
claims.text: With the conserved value, the defect of a round must disappear if the tape ends in a few periods I O O O and every digit before them is reached by many visits (b larger than a few times log2 k). Measured, b is at least 2m - 5 in the part rich in doublers; a proof of a lower bound is missing. It would show that the machine never halts. It follows if the digit-only end Z keeps at least k + 2 log2 k + 20 words, which needs the defect to reach Z in fewer than about half of the rounds; measured, a third. 22 November 2026: the digit end has four layers (see "Four layers of the digit end"), and only the bottom one, about 0.27 k irregular digits, is ever eaten. The three regular layers above it are about 1.6 k digits, so the lemma would follow from two statements: that the layers are always as observed (they come from the first two terms of the value), and that no defect crosses the whole irregular layer in one round. The second is still a statement about pseudo-random digits. Neither is proved.

claims.title: Token rules and the conserved value
claims.text: Taking the four visit functions A, E, F, P as the definition, every token rule (the counter rules for L, O, I, the rules of the travelling defect, and the re-readings at the blank end) is a computation of them, and none uses the halting case E(1 1 …). Every visit of A derived by these rules adds exactly 1 to the value v of the tape. That the machine's visits are these four functions is lean/Link.lean. That the rules apply to every tape with at most one defect is lean/Total.lean.

claims.title: A tape with at most one defect cannot halt
claims.text: The token rules are deterministic, and on every tape of words with at most one defect any number of visits of A in a row are derived by them, every tape in between again having at most one defect. At the bit level each of these visits is a computation of the four functions, none of which is the halting case E(1 1 …). So within a round the machine can halt only on a tape with two defects, which needs the defect of an earlier round to survive its round. This replaces the hand argument of the 14 November notes.

claims.title: The four visit functions are the machine
claims.text: Every computation of the visit functions A, E, F, P is a run of the transition table: a visit of X on the half tape from the head leftwards ends with the head just right of it in state B, for any tape to the right, which it never reads. One round takes 0 S (blank to the right, state A) to 0 1 0 A(S) the same way round, starting from blank tape with S = []. This replaces the check by c/zvis.cpp.

claims.title: If every defect dies, it never halts
claims.text: If in every round from blank tape the visit of A leaves a tape without defect, the machine never halts from blank tape. This hypothesis is now the whole open question.

claims.title: What the missing lemma really asks
claims.text: Followed over rounds 100 to 7,500, the defect gets into the digit-only end Z of the tape in only 32% of the rounds, and whether it does looks like an independent coin each round. When it gets in, it eats 4.8 words on average, about what random digits give (it crosses O and I I and stops at I O). Z gains 4 words per round and loses 2.15, so it stays near 1.85 k words, well above the k + 2 log<sub>2</sub> k + 20 the proof needs. So the lemma is not about a bias in the digits; it is about how rarely the defect gets past the part rich in doublers. One bad round can cost any amount, so this is a statement about pseudo-random digits, like Antihydra's. Under the random-digit model a defect survives a round with chance about 2<sup>-0.4k</sup>, below 2<sup>-40,000</sup> after round 100,000.

claims.title: Every defect followed for 500,000 rounds
claims.text: A new engine runs the token rules with each carry kept as a run-length coded bit string, the digit end of the tape as one big number, and the carries left after the defect has died walked together; it gives the same tape as py/tokz.py after every round (compared token for token at rounds 3,000, 8,000 and 30,000) about a thousand times faster. In each of the 500,000 rounds the defect died at 1 I O → O L inside the tape, long before the round ended (from round 13 on), and no two defects ever met. The largest carry of the last round has 944,371 bits, so the run covers more than 2944,371 (about 10284,283) steps of the machine. The visit engine's earlier record was 100,000 rounds.

claims.title: The defect over the long run
claims.text: From round 100 on the defect gets into the digit end Z in 30.8% of the rounds, a little less often right after rounds in which it did (27% after three in a row). There it eats 4.85 words on average, at most 60 (round 475,184), with a tail falling by about 0.81 per word, as random digits would give. Z loses 2.11 words per round and gains 4; the largest average loss over 100 rounds in a row is 2.88, over 1,000 rounds 2.33, over 10,000 rounds 2.19. From round 1,000 on |Z|/k stays between 1.73 and 1.89, and the margin of the lemma, |Z| − (k + 2 log<sub>2</sub> k + 20), is at least 699.

claims.title: The value at the start of a round, term by term
claims.text: With exact fractions up to round 420: v<sub>k</sub> = 1/15 − (290/127)·2<sup>−(k+2)/2</sup> + r<sub>k</sub> for even k and 1/15 − (288/127)·2<sup>−(k+1)/2</sup> + r<sub>k</sub> for odd k, with |r<sub>k</sub>| < 64·2<sup>−k</sup> from round 80 on. r<sub>k</sub>·2<sup>k</sup> settles to −33.6896… (even k) and −42.1256… (odd k), which are not small fractions, and still moves by about 2<sup>−k/2</sup>: the next term, of size 2<sup>−3k/2</sup>, is where the value stops being regular.

claims.title: Four layers of the digit end
claims.text: Read lowest digit first, the digit end Z of the tape is four layers (round 50,000; round 8,000 is alike). From the top: 24,996 digits of period 4 (the expansion of 1/15), 24,997 of period 28 (1/15 minus a multiple of 1/127), 29,782 digits that are the same in round 50,056 (frozen: once laid down they no longer change), and 13,402 irregular digits at the bottom. The regular layers are what the first two terms of the value predict; the defect only ever eats the irregular one, about 0.27 k digits.

claims.title: The twin's rounds on any tape
claims.text: Started in E on 0 0 0 1 0 S, the twin 1RB0LF_1LC1RC_0RA0LD_0LE1RE_0RF0LC_1RC--- reaches 0 0 0 1 0 1 0 A(S) for all 1,517 of 2,000 random tapes S (up to 30 cells) on which A(S) is defined, and halts on the other 483. Its visits close up on the token words with five entry forms, and every token rule is a run of the twin through them (symbolically). Since 22 November 2026 this is in Lean on the twin's own table: every token rule is a run of the twin from five entry forms, and the twin never halts under this machine's hypothesis (K83189.nonhalt_of_clean).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows whether it halts. Read in the words 1010, 000 and 100, its tape is a binary counter with doublers, and each round sends one defect through it. Lean proves that a tape with at most one defect never halts within a round, so a halt needs a defect that survives its round; in 500,000 rounds followed word by word, none did.

facts.text: A tape with at most one defect never halts within a round (lean/Total.lean).
Every defect followed word by word; each died about halfway into the tape (more than 2<sup>944,371</sup> steps).
The irregular bottom layer a defect would have to cross in one round.

sections.heading: A counter with doublers and a travelling defect
html: Read the tape from right to left in the words L = 1010, O = 000, I = 100. A visit of state A to a tape of such words is a counter step:
A(O W) = I W   A(I W) = O A(W)   A(L W) = L A(A(W))

O and I are binary digits, lowest first, and L is a doubler: a carry that crosses it becomes two carries. One round of the machine is S' = 1 0 A(S). The 1 0 put in front does not fit the words; it is a defect. Pushed by the carries, the defect travels through the counter, rewrites the words it crosses, and disappears where it turns 1 I O into O L, two digits into a doubler. Every round adds exactly four words.

A tape with at most one defect cannot halt (proved in Lean: lean/Total.lean). A halt needs two defects side by side, so the machine runs forever if every defect disappears before its round ends. In every round from 13 to 500,000 it did, about halfway into the tape (more than 2944,371 steps of the machine; the earlier visit engine reached 100,000 rounds). Where the defect disappears depends on the low digits of the counter, which look irregular: that is what a proof would have to control.

sections.heading: Four layers, and the only one the defect eats
html: The conserved value of the tape (each digit 1 counts 2−b, b = doublers minus digits before it) is known to high precision at the start of every round:
v = 1/15 − (290/127)·2−(k+2)/2 + C·2−k + …   (k even; 288/127 and 2−(k+1)/2 for k odd)

checked with exact fractions up to round 420. The far end of the tape holds the largest digits of v, so it is the binary expansion of these terms: first 1/15 = 0.000100010001… (period 4), then 1/15 minus a multiple of 1/127 (period 28), then digits that stay frozen from round to round. Below them, at the start of the digit-only end Z, sit the irregular digits where the terms no longer predict anything. Here is the tape of round 50,000, from the front (left) to the far end (right), in tokens:

So the question has moved. For the machine to halt, one defect would have to cross the whole irregular layer, about 0.27 k words (13,402 at round 50,000), in a single round, and then the regular layers above it. In 500,000 rounds the most it ever ate was 60 words. Nobody knows how to prove that the irregular digits never line up that way; it is the same kind of question as for Antihydra.

sections.heading: A binary counter at the left end
html: At an event the head is in state A just right of a fixed 14-cell word (the engine), and the tape reads
[left counter] 00101001010100 A> 0 [46-cell word] [M] …

The left counter is binary with 3-cell digits 000 = 0 and 100 = 1, most significant first; M is two 4-cell digits 1000 = 0, 1010 = 1. One event: the head runs right through the 46-cell word (the head turns at several places inside it, rewriting and then restoring it: it comes back unchanged), adds 1 to M, returns, carries 1 into the left counter, and comes back: 608 + 8k steps for a carry over k ones. Example (steps 100,465, 101,089, 101,705, 102,321, 102,979): the left counter reads 1000011, 1000100, 1000101, 1000110, 1000111 and M = 0, 1, 2, 3, 0.

Proved in Lean for every k (lean/Events.lean). Open: what the wrap of M does to the slower counter further right, and the occasional rebuilding of the 46-cell word, which is when the count of the left-end visits drops.

sections.heading: Visits to the left end
html: Every so often the head reaches the left end of the tape in state E, on blank. The tape then starts E>0 0 1 (0 0 1)^k 0 1 … and continues with single 1s separated by one, two or three 0s. From step 109,450,476 on (run of 109 steps):

The gaps between visits are 14.5, 29.0, 57.9 million steps: they double, apart from some shorter ones where a carry stops early. Earlier the front went up to 14 (step 3,688,357), dropped to 8, went up to 11, dropped to 9, rose to 12, dropped to 11, and climbed to 18 (step 94,782,615) before dropping to 2.

sections.heading: Sweeps
html: The head crosses repeated words in one state, rewriting each copy the same way: for example A turns 0 1 into 1 0 and B turns 1 0 0 into 0 0 0. These rules are proved in Lean for any number of copies: a_right_01, a_right_001, b_right_10, b_right_100, c_right_10, d_right_01.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The machine halts only when D reads a 1. A closed tape language with windows of six cells (an over-approximation of the configurations reachable from blank tape, found by bbtools.ctl) allows that only at the left end of the tape, with 100100, 100101, 101001 or 101010 from the head on. Whether the counter ever leaves that pattern at the front when D arrives is the open question.

sections.heading: Next steps
html: Read the gaps as digits, write what one visit does to them and when the front collapses, and check the rule against the visits of a longer run; then find which value of the counter puts D on a 1 at the left end.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.08). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 275 cells (222 left of the start, 46 right), with a density of 1s of 0.309.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Binary counter with doublers (words 1010, 000, 100) and one travelling defect per round; Lean: the visit functions are the machine, a tape with at most one defect cannot halt, and if every round's defect dies the machine never halts; every defect followed for 500,000 rounds; open: that every defect disappears before its round ends.
